Root cause suspected to be tied to the recent Delhaize/ADUSA unification changes — new user accounts are provisioning without a default hierarchy assignment, which blocks store-location selection at case creation. Requesting Eng review of the user-provisioning/hierarchy sync impacted by the unification — need to confirm whether this is a one-time backfill issue for already-migrated ADUSA users or an ongoing default-assignment bug for all new users going forward. Thanks

","created":"2026-09-02T03:03:07.942-0400","updated":"2026-09-02T03:03:07.942-0400","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"712020:d9560df8-4bed-43ed-83aa-ec4980ed1454","displayName":"Megha Rathi"},"jsdPublic":false},{"id":"3326604","author":{"accountId":"712020:688bd119-6d13-450b-95ac-b1ef3fbb547b","displayName":"Juan Martinez"},"body":"

Environment: Production, AHL/DLZ tenant, Delhaize brands.

Steps to reproduce:

  1. Provision a new LPMS user for a Delhaize brand employee through the standard flow, with no manual hierarchy assignment.

  2. Sign in as that user.

  3. Attempt to select a store location to open a case.

Expected: the user has a hierarchy location available and can select a store. Actual: no hierarchy is present. The location selector is empty and the user cannot start a case. Confirmed against Gabriel Quist, the ticket reporter, 8/29.

Findings: Same symptom as RCS-28415 and RCS-28519, both closed by manually correcting the affected account. Three reports on the same provisioning path point at how new accounts arrive, not at three isolated accounts.

Root cause suspected, per Megha Rathi's note on 9/2: the Delhaize unification change leaves new user accounts without a default hierarchy assignment on provisioning. Not yet confirmed in code.

Troubleshooting performed: Manual workaround applied for Gabriel Quist on 8/29, adding a hierarchy location by hand. That unblocked him. No automated fix attempted. No AI assisted troubleshooting used on this ticket beyond drafting this note. No conversation with engineers occurred outside this ticket.

Still open:

  1. Confirm whether hierarchy assignment for a new user should come from the SSO claim or the store file at provisioning time, or whether it is a client administration task. This decides the classification.

  2. Please clone this into an ENG ticket and link it back here. Ticket is 5 days old with no defect ticket created yet.

","created":"2026-09-24T10:45:28.690-0400","updated":"2026-09-24T10:45:28.690-0400","updateAuthor":{"accountId":"6201ac57e5caff0070e1e981","displayName":"Kiran Vadday"},"jsdPublic":false},{"id":"3362968","author":{"accountId":"712020:688bd119-6d13-450b-95ac-b1ef3fbb547b","displayName":"Juan Martinez"},"body":"

Hi @leighann.stubbs@adusa.com

Thank you for sending the Gabriel Quist examples and for confirming he could create cases once the hierarchy was in place. That made this much easier to review with our engineering team.

To answer your question, our engineering team confirmed that assigning a hierarchy to a new user is an administrator task. The platform does not assign one when a user account is created, so each new user needs at least one hierarchy assignment before they can select a store and start a case.

The steps you followed for Gabriel are the correct process. From Settings > Users, select the user, click Edit and open the Hierarchies tab. Choose Standard Location Hierarchy, then the level that matches the user's scope, such as Location for a single store or District for a whole district. Pick the store or district under Select Locations, click Add, and then click Save at the top of the page. The assignment shows up under Members on the same tab, and the user can select that location the next time they sign in. I have attached two screenshots of the Hierarchies tab for reference.

It may help to add this step to your onboarding checklist for new users, so nobody gets stuck on their first case. If any user still cannot select a location after a hierarchy has been assigned, just reply here and I will look into that account directly.

Thank you again for your patience on this one.

Kind Regards,
Appriss Retail Support

EXTERNAL SENDER

Upon hiring, the user’s manager must submit a request to be granted a role into LPMS with our IT department. Upon my approval of the request, I give IT the proper role to assign to the user. Those roles determine what access they have to the system. A user is provisioned by Brand/Division; not a single location or district.

Upon the email they receive stating they are granted access to LPMS with a 4-6 hour waiting period due to synching. Now we have to wait until they log into the system to determine that they can’t even create a case. This has not been an issue until now.

There has to be a better way.

Leigh Ann Stubbs
Administrator, Corporate Asset Protection

Hi @leighann.stubbs@adusa.com

Thank you for explaining how new user requests move through your IT team and how access is granted by Brand/Division. That helps me see exactly where the extra step lands for you.

Before we suggest a change, I would like to make sure I understand the full flow. Would you be open to a short call so you can walk me through it, from the manager's request to the user's first login? Just let me know what time works best for you and I will fit it in.

In the meantime, one option that may help: when an administrator creates a new user, the permission groups, hierarchy and security level can all be set in the same step. The account can stay disabled until IT confirms the approval, and then be enabled, so the user has everything in place at first login.

Thank you again for your patience on this one.

Kind Regards,
Appriss Retail Support
